svg.title: If γ = 0, direct and iterated coefficients already have the common raw rate, so their difference has that rate by the triangle inequality; no high-accuracy replacement is needed at a zero exponent gap. If there are no nonroot internal vertices, there is one choice at every child, its coefficient is 1, and permutation invariance identifies the parent sum with the direct coefficient exactly. Take γ to be the minimum of the finitely many (Dv + 1)∆v. Choose a vertex attaining this minimum. Its ratio power qDv+1 has rate −γ, while the positive slack in (NE1) absorbs the fixed v constants in (NE6). Its single positive ratio term is bounded by the sum in (NE2), proving the claimed sum of gains. The direct coefficient and exterior remainder rates similarly give (NE2)’s first inequality and (NE3). Contractivity and the character supremum give the latter in the common ground-algebra norm.
